name: openstatus-mcp
cost: Self-hosting is open source (AGPL-3.0). The managed service has flat pricing; amounts not stated in the README
works_with: Any MCP client, including Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex, opencode and VS Code
short: Lets your agent read your openstatus monitors and post or resolve incidents, status updates and maintenance windows.
what: A skill that teaches your agent to use the openstatus MCP server, a remote endpoint with 23 tools. Your agent can check monitor health and latency, read response logs, notification channels and audit logs, and open, update and resolve status reports or schedule maintenance on your status pages. It can also search the openstatus docs and pricing pages.
who: Teams that already use openstatus for uptime monitoring and status pages and want to run incidents from their agent. If you don't use openstatus, this skill does nothing for you.
needs: For headless use: an openstatus API key from Settings > General

steps.title: Connect with OAuth
steps.text: Point your client at the endpoint. It opens a consent screen where you choose the workspace and read-only or read & write access.
steps.code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user openstatus https://api.openstatus.dev/mcp

steps.title: Or add it to another client's config
For CI or headless agents
steps.text: Send an API key in the `x-openstatus-key` header in the same config. A key's scope is fixed when you create it.

steps.title: Ask your agent
steps.text: Ask about a monitor's health, or to post an incident. Before any publishing call it should show you a draft and ask whether to notify subscribers.

try.label: From the SKILL.md
try.text: Ask it to check a monitor's health, then to post an update on an open incident and resolve it.

watch: Read & write access lets your agent publish incidents and maintenance windows. Choose read-only on the consent screen if you only want to look.
Notifications go out inside the same call. An update posted with `notify: false` can never be re-sent later.
Every MCP change is written to the workspace audit log with the key or OAuth grant and the person behind it.
Connected apps can be revoked under Settings > Integrations > Connected apps.
Two audit-log tools need the `audit-log` plan feature.
